paper.title: Self-organized criticality: An explanation of the 1/f noise

headline: BTW sandpile (cellular automaton / SOC): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; fitted tau=1.261 (kmin=1), nonzero sizes span 4.0 decades (max/median=414x), stationary mean height=2.098

verdicts.gate: P1 fitted tail exponent tau in [0.9, 1.6] (power-law avalanche sizes, BTW 2D tau~1.2)
P2 heavy-tailed: nonzero sizes span >= 2.0 decades AND max >= 100.0x median nonzero
P3 stationary mean height in [2.0, 2.2] (self-organized critical state)

extra.fit_method: exact discrete power-law MLE (zeta-likelihood; Clauset et al. 2009), kmin=1
extra.model_class: cellular automaton / self-organized criticality (NOT agent-stepping ABM): a deterministic toppling rule is applied to a grid of integer heights; there are no agents, no scheduler, no per-agent decisions
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic CA/SOC result; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the SOC power-law (tau~1.2) and would catch an artifact (e.g. a non-power-law or wrong critical mean height)

citations: Bak, P., Tang, C. & Wiesenfeld, K. (1987). Self-organized criticality: An explanation of the 1/f noise. Phys. Rev. Lett. 59:381-384. doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.59.381.
Clauset, A., Shalizi, C.R. & Newman, M.E.J. (2009). Power-law distributions in empirical data. SIAM Review 51(4):661-703 (discrete-MLE estimator).

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction. Canonical 2D BTW exponent tau~1.2 serves as the literature anchor (P1).
